title: Burning Steppes
body: The Burning Steppes were green country once, the northern reaches of the Redridge Mountains, until exiled Dark Iron dwarves raised their capital of Thaurissan here. When Sorcerer-Thane Thaurissan called up Ragnaros the Firelord, mountains melted, Blackrock Mountain was born and the land was burned to ash. The sky still glows red above rivers of lava and charred earth. In the Second War the Horde made the mountain its stronghold, and at its foot Orgrim Doomhammer slew Anduin Lothar. Now the Blackrock orcs hold the steppes again, mining the hills for the metal of their weapons, and those who have seen inside their citadel say the clan answers to the black dragonflight, whose dragonkin swarm the eastern valleys. Firegut ogres guard Dreadmaul Rock for them, and Dark Iron agents prowl the ruins of the ancient city. Against all this stand only a few: the Alliance soldiers of Morgan's Vigil in the southeast, and an odd company of goblins, scholars and Horde fliers at Flame Crest.

title: Blackrock Pass
body: Blackrock Pass is the road by which most travelers from the lands of Stormwind reach the Burning Steppes, climbing north out of the Redridge Mountains past the Blackrock camp that watches its southern end. The change on crossing is abrupt. Behind lie green slopes and the lake country around Lakeshire; ahead the earth is black and cracked and the air shimmers with heat. Living fire haunts the pass itself. Flamekin spitters and sprites, small elementals of flame, drift among the rocks, lava crabs scuttle through the cinders, and an elemental of obsidian lumbers along the road toward Morgan's Vigil.

title: Morgan's Vigil
body: On a ridge in the southeastern corner of the steppes, a small company of the Alliance keeps watch from among the scarred ruins of an older town. Morgan's Vigil is the Alliance's only foothold in this land, and a modest one: an innkeeper, a weaponsmith and a dwarven gryphon master whose birds fly to Stormwind, Lakeshire and Thorium Point. Marshal Maxwell commands, joined by the night elf Helendis Riverhorn, the gnome mage Jalinda Sprig, the priestess Mayara Brightwing and the half-mad dwarf Oralius. Their fight is Lakeshire's fight too. The Blackrock clan the Vigil watches day and night is the same that crossed the mountains to raid Redridge, and dragonkin roam the valley to the north.

title: Dreadmaul Rock
body: Dreadmaul Rock is a great crag in the east of the steppes, riddled with caves and old mines and held by the Firegut ogres. They are allies of the Blackrock orcs, guarding the rock's rich mineral seams and keeping the clan's supply lines open. Ogre-mages and brutes crowd its slopes, and the hulking Hahk'Zor and Gorgon'och stalk among them. Something darker goes on in the caves. Reports of strange rituals among the ogres drew a Horde patrol here weeks ago, and no word has come back from it. Fire elementals and lava crabs creep over the lower slopes, and the molten giant Volchan is sometimes seen wandering near its foot.

title: Terror Wing Path
body: North of Morgan's Vigil a long valley runs up the eastern edge of the steppes, and it belongs to the black dragonflight. Dragonspawn and wyrmkin patrol the Terror Wing Path in numbers, broodlings swarm underfoot, and black drakes prowl among them. Even seasoned travelers are warned not to come alone. Other hunters share the valley: venomtip scorpids, ember worgs and the great worg Deathmaw, Firegut ogres straying from Dreadmaul Rock, and malfunctioning war golems that lurch through the ash. At the valley's far northern end lies Slither Rock, the lair of the dragonspawn Cyrus Therepentous.

title: Slither Rock
body: In the far northeastern corner of the steppes, beyond the Terror Wing Path, a small cave opens in the rock. Few go there willingly. Slither Rock is the lair of a single great servant of the black dragonflight, the dragonspawn Cyrus Therepentous, and black broodlings scuttle near its mouth. Cyrus answers most visitors with contempt and a threat to devour them, yet those who prove themselves useful may leave with a bargain instead. For all his scorn, he will help a mortal against a foe they share, so long as it feeds his own hunger.

title: Flame Crest
body: Flame Crest is a rocky outcrop in the north of the steppes, reached by a crude bridge, with a small cave at its back. No kingdom rules it. Goblins and wandering scholars do business here: Tinkee Steamboil studies the local dragonkin, Kibler sells exotic pets from the cave, Yuka Screwspigot hunts for her worthless brother, and Maxwort Uberglint chases the lost treasures of the Dark Irons. The elven mage Mathredis Firestar seeks the librams scattered when the Scourge struck Quel'Thalas, and the drunken dwarf Ragged John wanders in from his jaunts to the Spire. The Horde keeps a foothold too, a wind rider master and a provisioner who serve its people in this hostile land.

title: Ruins of Thaurissan
body: In the heart of the steppes lie the broken streets of Thaurissan, once capital of the Dark Iron dwarves, destroyed when their sorcerer-thane called Ragnaros into the world. The Dark Irons have not given it up. Thaurissan spies, agents and firewalkers stalk the rubble beside iron war reavers, and a rare Dark Iron named Thauris Balgarr walks among them. Relics still lie in the ash. Touch one and a tormented voice may warn the intruder away as visions burn into the mind: eight dwarves at a ritual, a lone dwarf kneeling before a monolith of flame among seven corpses. Treasure hunters come regardless, drawn by rumors of a Tablet of the Seven.

title: The Pillar of Ash
body: South of the ruined city, out on the open plain, the Blackrock clan keeps the Pillar of Ash, one of its camps in the heart of the steppes. Slayers and soldiers stand guard, sorcerers and warlocks work their dark craft, and worgs bred in the Spire pace at their masters' heels. The orcs carry medallions of the clan, and those badges have become trophies: at Morgan's Vigil, the mad dwarf Oralius wants them by the fifty. Further west, more Blackrock camps dot the plain.

title: Blackrock Stronghold
body: In the north of the steppes, just outside Blackrock Spire, the Blackrock clan has raised a great fortress, hidden from the road but always watching for an Alliance attack. Battlemasters, slayers and warlocks man its walls, sentries and grunts of the Scarshield Legion stand among them, and the orc Gruklash, prone to fits of frenzy, prowls the grounds. The fortress shelters friends of the clan as well. Grark Lorkrub, who betrayed the Kargath Expeditionary Force to the Blackrock, waits here under their protection, sure that no enemy could slip into so heavily fortified a place to take him.

title: Blackrock Mountain
body: The northwestern sky of the steppes belongs to Blackrock Mountain, the volcano raised by Ragnaros's coming, and the road from the Steppes climbs straight to it. Dragonkin of the black flight hold its southern slopes, flamescale dragonspawn and wyrmkin among them, and great Blackrock drakes keep watch with them. Within the mountain the Dark Irons rule the depths and the Blackrock clan the Spire above, while orcs of the Scarshield Legion stand sentry on the slopes. Strange figures linger here. The ghost of Franclorn Forgewright, the dwarf who built the Spire, haunts his own tomb at its gate, and Lothos Riftwaker speaks of the rifts that tear the fabric of the world.

title: Altar of Storms
body: In the far west of the steppes, in the shadow of Blackrock Spire, stands the Altar of Storms, where Blackrock warlocks gather for strange rituals. They have unusual neighbors. Just beside the altar a human warlock, Mor'zul Bloodbringer, keeps a camp of his own, studying the place and perhaps hoping to harness its power. Warlocks of great skill seek him out, for he knows the rites that can bind a dreadsteed from the burning Plains of Xoroth, though the price is paid in blood, sweat and gold. His servant Gorzeeki Wildeyes, a gifted alchemist, prepares the ink and other trappings such work demands, and has a taste for spiders and beetles.

title: Draco'dar
body: Draco'dar is a stretch of scorched hills in the southwest of the steppes, crawling with servants of the black dragonflight. Flamescale broodlings tumble among the rocks, searscale drakes hunt the slopes, and the rare black drake Hematos is sometimes seen there, breathing fire on whatever moves. Giant ember worgs and firetail scorpids prowl the ash. Amid all this danger one man seems entirely at ease: Franklin the Friendly, a smiling stranger who urges passers-by to pay no mind to the lava and take in the joys that nature has to offer. How he lives so contentedly in such a place, he does not say.

title: Marshal Maxwell
body: Marshal Maxwell commands the soldiers of Morgan's Vigil, Stormwind's only outpost in the Burning Steppes. The Vigil has paid dearly for its post. Its commanding officer, Marshal Windsor, vanished when a Blackrock raiding party fell upon him, and a great store of intelligence on the clan went with him. Maxwell sees his war as one of two fronts: one is fought from Stormwind itself, while the Vigil carries the battle to the black dragonflight's doorstep. He has no doubt who stands behind the orcs, and none of the enemy, he vows, will be spared, as none of his own were spared when they struck at the homes and families of the Alliance.

parts.body: Ragged John's tale changed everything. If the drunkard was to be believed, Windsor still lived, taken prisoner and dragged off into Blackrock Depths. Maxwell called John a good for nothing coward, and sent a deputy into the Dark Iron city all the same: if Windsor was alive, bring him back, and if he was dead, bring proof.

parts.body: The marshal was found in a Dark Iron cell, but not as Maxwell remembered him. Windsor raged that Bolvar was a blind fool who could not see the proof in front of him, that his own information was lost for good, and that he would carry his hammer to Stormwind himself. Hearing it, Maxwell lowered his head in mourning for a proud and noble warrior turned into a raving wreck. It seemed a dead end.
sources: quest 4242 description (Windsor in Blackrock Depths) and reward text (gone mad, Maxwell lowers his head in mourning, a dead end)

parts.body: It was not the end. With his lost information torn back from the Dark Irons and his gear recovered, Windsor broke out of the Depths and stormed through the Vigil, making grand claims he swore his evidence would prove. Then he was gone, bound for Stormwind to confront Highlord Bolvar and Lady Prestor, and Maxwell's orders to those who would follow were plain: gather an army and meet the marshal at the gates of the city.

parts.body: Word of the enemy's true master reached the Vigil by an unlikely road: a marked map from Bijou, a goblin spying for the Horde inside Blackrock Spire. The orcs, she reported, are beasts of burden and cannon fodder for the black dragonflight, and their true leader is Nefarian, brood of Deathwing. It matched much of what Maxwell already knew. With her markings he planned his strikes: the war master Voone, then the ogre Highlord Omokk, then the overlord Wyrmthalak.

parts.body: From the fallen overlord came a letter on protocol from his superior, General Drakkisath. The plot thickens, Maxwell said, and he named his next target: the general himself. The task would not be a simple one, he warned, but the rewards would be extravagant.

title: Helendis Riverhorn
body: Helendis Riverhorn is a night elf who serves the Alliance at Morgan's Vigil, far from the forests of his people, and still asks the blessing of Cenarius on those he sends into danger. He has studied the enemy closely. The worgs the Blackrock orcs command never seem to dwindle, however many are slain, and his scouts have traced them to Blackrock Spire, where they are bred, trained and sent out to the clan. Whatever lies at the root of it, the orcs know it by a single name: Halycon. Like his comrades at the Vigil, he suspects the orcs themselves are pawns of the black dragonflight, which feeds their rage.

parts.body: The source of the worgs was a she-worg, Halycon, kept deep in the Spire. When she was dead, Helendis asked that no one dwell on her suffering. The beast had been corrupt, he said, a product of dark magic, and ending her was a great service to the Alliance.
sources: quest 4701 reward text (do not dwell upon her suffering; corrupt, a product of dark magic; a great service to the Alliance)
quest 4701 log (Halycon, the name the orcs use for the worg)

title: Oralius
body: Oralius is a dwarf soldier of Morgan's Vigil, and something in him has broken. He barks at every visitor as if at a raw recruit, cackles over his battle plans, and shouts, as a great confidence, that he is the only sane one left in the camp. His constant companion is Captain Winky, a friend no one else can see, with whom he argues, plots and on occasion trades a pirate's growl. He keeps a collection of severed ogre ears, and into one of them he calls out reports to some distant control. Mad or not, he wages his own war on the Firegut ogres and the Blackrock with deadly seriousness.
sources: quest 4283 description and request text (only sane one, Captain Winky, ogre ear collection, talking into a severed ogre ear: Burning Steppes to control)
quests 3823, 3824 (Winky outbursts), 4286 (pirate impersonation)

title: Mayara Brightwing
body: Mayara Brightwing is a priestess in the service of Count Remington Ridgewell of Stormwind's House of Nobles, who sent her to the Burning Steppes to scout the ruins of Thaurissan for treasures worthy of his family museum. Her search has led beyond the ruins, into Blackrock Spire. High in the citadel lies a chamber once called the Hall of Fortune, where the Dark Irons kept their relics, trophies and works of art, before it collapsed and fell to darker uses. Among its lost treasures is Doomrigger's Clasp, so encrusted with gems that it was said to make any dwarf who gazed upon it weep, and Mayara means to have it.
sources: quest 4766 description (Ridgewell's agent sent to scout Thaurissan for the family museum)

title: Ragged John
body: Ragged John is a dwarf of Flame Crest who is rarely, if ever, entirely sober. The soldiers of Morgan's Vigil remember that he was with their commander, Marshal Windsor, when a Blackrock raiding party fell upon them, and that he came back when Windsor did not. These days he makes his own jaunts into Blackrock Spire, where he has overheard the orcs speak of a poison they call Mother's Milk, after the great spider Mother Smolderweb. Ragged John wants a sample, still flowing in the veins of someone brave or foolish enough to be bitten. He swears it is not for poisoning anyone: it will make the best ale yet.
sources: npc_text 2713 (What you be wanting? *hic*)
quest 4866 description and reward text

parts.body: Pressed on official business, John at last tells of Windsor's last stand. Deep in Blackrock Mountain the orcs rushed them. John slipped into the shadows while Windsor held his ground for hours, swinging Ironfoe, a hammer Franclorn Forgewright made for the marshal's forebear. He came through it alive, drenched in orc blood, only for some three hundred Dark Irons to take him prisoner. Their leader kept Ironfoe, and Windsor, John figures, is somewhere in Blackrock Depths.
sources: npc_text 2714-2723, 2725 (Ragged John's tale: Ironfoe, fifty orcs, slipped into the shadows, three hundred Dark Irons, prisoner, their leader took Ironfoe, somewhere in Blackrock Depths)

title: Cyrus Therepentous
body: Cyrus Therepentous is a black dragonspawn who keeps to his lair at Slither Rock and holds every mortal in contempt. Only a fool, he says, would disturb him there, and those who do are left to wonder whether he will devour them whole or let them live. Yet he finds uses for lesser beings. Those who seek out his flight he sends to challenge his minion, and any who survive and return with proof of their victory have shown, in his eyes, that they are not entirely useless.
sources: npc_text 2493, 2494 (lair, devour you whole, challenge my minion)
quests 4022, 4023, 4024 (descriptions, logs and reward texts; Altered Black Dragonflight Molt)

parts.body: Some visitors Cyrus knows before they speak. The flight is aware of their work in the Searing Gorge, he tells them, and he demands to see the molt they were given there by one of his kin.

parts.body: Once satisfied, Cyrus names what he craves: the molten fire of Blackrock Mountain. In the depths below dwells Bael'Gar, a being of pure flame born of the fires of Ragnaros, and Cyrus hungers for his inner flame. He has altered a molt of his flight so that it can safely draw that fire from the giant's smoldering remains.

title: Tinkee Steamboil
body: Tinkee Steamboil is a goblin scholar who has spent weeks at Flame Crest studying the dragonkin of the Burning Steppes. The land is dangerous, she admits, but scholars like her will do almost anything to advance their knowledge. Her inventions carry names as bold as her ambitions: the Draco Incarcinatrix 900, which draws the essence from a slain broodling, and the eggscilloscope, built to freeze a dragon's egg solid. She dreams of being the envy of dragon scholars around the world. Tinkee does not work for herself alone. Her research answers to a patron she calls her master, one she warns is not the sort anyone should wish to disappoint.
sources: npc_text 3296 (dangerous place, scholars like me)

title: Kibler
body: Kibler is a goblin animal lover by inclination and a salesman by trade. From his cave at Flame Crest, crowded with cages, he tracks down exotic beasts for the rich and famous and tames them into proper pets, from worg pups taken out of Blackrock Spire to the spiders that hatch from its eggs. He pays others to take the risks. One of them, the goblin Bijou, went into the Spire after its spider eggs weeks ago and has not been heard from since. His parrot Opus squawks his secrets to anyone who listens: that Bijou is lost, that dragons control the orcs, and that Kibler is under investigation by something called G.E.T.A.
sources: quest 4729 description (animal lover, salesman, exotic animals for the rich and famous, cages)

parts.body: Bijou was more than Kibler's hireling. Found deep in Blackrock Spire, she proved to be an agent of the Horde on a mission of the utmost importance to her masters, spying on the Blackrock orcs. What she had learned, she judged, mattered to the Alliance as well, and she traded it for help recovering her lost belongings.

quest 5001 description (mission of utmost importance to the Horde; information useful to the Alliance in exchange for her belongings)
quest 5002 description

parts.body: Bijou was more than Kibler's hireling. At Kargath, Grandmaster Lexlort counts her among the slipperiest operatives of the Kargath Expeditionary Force, and he is not pleased: she has been two-timing the Horde, working on the side for the pet dealer and paying for her errands with Horde funds. She was last seen entering Blackrock Spire, and Lexlort wants her brought back alive.
sources: quest 4981 description (one of our slipperiest operatives, working for Kibler, two timing us, using Horde funds, last seen entering Blackrock Spire, bring her back alive), given by Lexlort 9080 (Kargath Expeditionary Force) at Kargath, no prerequisite

title: The Firegut Offensive
body: Oralius of Morgan's Vigil has a plan of attack, and he means to carry it out in phases. The Firegut ogres of Dreadmaul Rock are allies of the Blackrock orcs, guarding the rock's rich minerals and keeping the clan's supply lines open at all times, so the first blow must cripple their numbers: ogre-mages, ogres and brutes alike. He gives his orders like a drill sergeant, then breaks off to throttle the empty air and threaten his invisible friend Winky. Blood on the uniform, he insists, is the true measure of a soldier's work.
sources: quests 3823, 3824, 3825 (descriptions, logs and reward texts)
gameobject 160840 Soft Dirt Mound at Dreadmaul Rock (area 249)
DB: Gor'tesh 9176 at -8110,-1418 (generic area 46, west of Dreadmaul Rock)

'Comes in three phases' softened to 'in phases', since the third phase is first named in 3824. Earlier: verified. Alliance only (AllowableRaces 1101). Gor'tesh is not given a KILL trigger to keep one entry point.

parts.body: With the ogres reeling, for minutes, maybe even hours, Oralius calls for the decisive strike. Gor'tesh, the brute lord, rules the ogres not from Dreadmaul Rock but from a Blackrock structure to its west, and Oralius wants his fat head brought back to prepare the third phase of the attack.
sources: quest 3823 reward text
quest 3824 description, offered on the turn-in of 3823 (RewardNextQuest)

parts.body: The third phase is pure theater. Oralius mounts the head on a pike and sends it to be planted on the summit of Dreadmaul Rock, certain that the sight of that disgusting mug will send the cowardly ogres running for their lives in mass hysteria. He cackles wildly at the thought, and seems to be losing his grip on reality.
sources: quest 3824 reward text
quest 3825 description, offered on the turn-in of 3824 (RewardNextQuest)

parts.body: With the pike planted on the summit, Oralius is beside himself, and wants to know whether anyone painted pictures of the event. He will surely get the medal of bravery for this, he exclaims, then corrects himself: the soldier, of course, will be the one rewarded handsomely.
sources: quest 3825 completion and reward texts

title: The Fate of Sha'ni Proudtusk
body: Sha'ni Proudtusk of the Kargath Expeditionary Force went into the Burning Steppes with her platoon to look into reports of strange ritual activity among the Firegut ogres. More than three weeks later there is still no word. Warlord Goretooth has told her husband, Thal'trak, that no one in the platoon has been heard from and that he should move on and attend to the task at hand. Thal'trak cannot leave his post at Kargath, and he cannot let her go either. She is his wife, and he begs for someone to search for her.
sources: quests 3821, 3822 (descriptions, logs and reward texts)
creature_queststarter: Thal'trak Proudtusk 9082 (Kargath Expeditionary Force) starts 3821; Sha'ni Proudtusk 9136 ends 3821 and starts 3822
gameobject 160445 Sha'ni Proudtusk's Remains and Krom'Grul 8977 in area 249
notes: Converted: the opening is Thal'trak's plea (3821 description). Earlier: verified. Horde only (AllowableRaces 690). 3821 is filed under Badlands but the Badlands file does not use it; Goretooth's line overlaps lightly with Badlands 322 only as a mention.

parts.body: Her remains were found at Dreadmaul Rock, and her spirit told the rest. The whole platoon had been captured and slain, all but Sha'ni, whom the ogre Krom'Grul kept for some ritual. Chained to an altar, she was tortured until her body gave out, and the beast tore her wedding nose-ring from her face and wore it on his finger. Her grief was for Thal'trak: once their tours were over, they were to make a home with her parents in the Hinterlands.
sources: quest 3821 reward text (plans to move in with her parents in the Hinterlands)
quest 3822 description (platoon captured and slain, ritual, altar, torture, nose-ring on his finger), offered by Sha'ni on the turn-in of 3821 (RewardNextQuest)

parts.body: When the ring came back to Kargath with her promise that they would meet again in another life, Thal'trak collapsed. This was to have been her last mission, he sobbed, and he would not take the ring. Without her, it meant nothing to him.
sources: quest 3822 description (tell him we will meet again in another life) and reward text

title: The Traitor of Kargath
body: Grandmaster Lexlort, head of the Kargath Expeditionary Force's reconnaissance, tracked one of the Horde's own across the Searing Gorge, through Blackrock Mountain and into the Burning Steppes. The traitor, Grark Lorkrub, was caught red-handed passing word of the force's daily operations to the Blackrock orcs, and now sits in their great fortress believing himself safe under their protection. Lexlort's answer is a set of thorium shackles. Grark is to be bound and led back through the mountain to the Searing Gorge, where Lexlort's men will be waiting to take him into custody.
sources: quest 4122 description, log and reward text

They do come, again and again along the road through the mountain.

title: Eggs of the Black Flight
body: Tinkee Steamboil has spent weeks at Flame Crest studying the dragonkin of the Burning Steppes, and she believes she has made a breakthrough. Her Draco Incarcinatrix 900 is meant to capture the essence of black broodlings: zap one with the device, slay it while the effect holds, and its essence should be released for study. If that works, she dreams, one day she might capture living whelps or even their eggs, and be the envy of dragon scholars around the world. Her patron, she warns, is not the sort anyone should wish to disappoint.
sources: quests 4726, 4808, 4809, 4810, 4734, 4735, 5522 (descriptions and reward texts)
quest 4771 description (Vectus, undead mage leading Scourge scholars in Scholomance)
warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Tinkee_Steamboil (Vectus her master)
notes: Converted: the opening is the setup of 4726 (its description and reward text, the patron warning from its completion text). Felnok's parts moved to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 4726, offering 4808); the eggscilloscope and the harvest to part 2 (QUEST_DONE 4735, turned in to Tinkee); Leonid's letter to part 3 (QUEST_ACCEPT 5522, filed under this zone); the trick to part 4 (QUEST_DONE 5522). 'Vectus an undead mage in Scholomance' is trimmed to 'serves the Scourge', since his Scholomance post is told only in 4771, offered by Betina Bigglezink in the Eastern Plaguelands. The Dawn's Gambit sequel stays with Scholomance. Earlier: verified. Faction 0: every quest in the chain has AllowableRaces 0. The Dawn's Gambit sequel in Scholomance is left to that dungeon.

parts.body: The essence told her that dragon eggs might be frozen and preserved. For that she needed special components from her colleague Felnok Steelspring in distant Everlook, and Felnok in turn needed pristine horns from the chillwind chimaerae of Winterspring, packed with cold, before he could send the package on.
sources: quest 4808 description, offered on the turn-in of 4726 (RewardNextQuest)
quests 4809, 4810 descriptions

parts.body: With Felnok's parts she built the eggscilloscope, made to freeze a black dragon's egg solid, and it was proven in the dragons' rookery high in Blackrock Spire. A collectronic module carried the frozen eggs away. Tinkee was delighted, and so, she said, would her patron be, for he had heard of the work and was very eager to get his hands on them.
sources: quest 4734 description and reward text
quest 4735 description, completion and reward texts (my patron is very eager to get his hands on them)

parts.body: Then a message came for Tinkee, meant to be from her master, Vectus, though it was signed by one Leonid Barthalomew. No one knows her master unless he allows it, so she did as she was told and sent the eggs to Leonid at Light's Hope Chapel in the Eastern Plaguelands, hurt only that Vectus had not trusted her to bring them herself.
sources: quest 5522 description

parts.body: It was a trick. Leonid, called the Revered by his brethren of the Argent Dawn, is no servant of Tinkee's master. The eggs were meant for the Scourge, whose experiments sought to create a plagued dragonflight, and had they reached their destination a great power would have fallen into the hands of the enemy. Vectus, it follows, serves the Scourge.
sources: quest 5522 reward text (I am no servant of that master; known as the Revered to my brethren in the Argent Dawn; a great power would have fallen into the hands of the enemy)
quest 5531 description (Scourge experiments to create a plagued dragonflight), offered by Leonid on the turn-in of 5522 (RewardNextQuest)
